contractSource: Description: "Simulate sunlight exposure on buildings... Visualize sun position..." Surface Type: Wall / Roof / Ground; Orientation slider 0–360° (180° = S).
groundTruth: Solar declination (Cooper 1969): δ = 23.45° × sin(360/365 × (284 + n)). Solar elevation at solar noon = 90° − |φ − δ|. Direct beam on a vertical wall is proportional to cos(elevation) × cos(sun azimuth − wall azimuth), and is zero when the sun is behind the wall.

cases.derivation: 20 March 2026 is day n = 79: δ = 23.45 × sin(360/365 × 363) = 23.45 × sin(358.03°) = −0.81°. At latitude 40°N at 12:00 solar time the sun is due south at elevation 90 − (40 + 0.81) = 49.2°. A wall facing north (orientation 0°) has the sun directly behind it: no direct sunlight, 0% exposure.

Same sun (elevation 49.2°, azimuth 180°). A south-facing wall (180°) meets the beam head-on in azimuth, so its incidence factor is cos(49.2°) × cos(0°) = 0.653 → about 65%. (sin 49.2° = 0.757 would be the factor for a horizontal roof, not a vertical wall.)
